questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error,select 'No Error'.**

Several visitors are (1)/ expected to visit the (2)/ trade fair this weekend. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

There is no grammatical error in above mentioned sentence. Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error,select 'No Error'.**

Our professor taught us that (1)/ one should respect the (2)/ religions of others as much as his own. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3, i.e. error lies in this part.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the **incorrect usage of the pronoun 'his'.**
 
• The** possessive pronoun 'his' **needs to be replaced with **possessive pronoun 'one's'.**
 
• The word** ‘one’ ** act as an **indefinite pronoun or impersonal pronoun** in the English language.
 
• ​ It is a **gender-neutral, third-person singular pronoun.** 
 
• When** 'One'** is used as the subject then its **objective case** i.e.** 'one'**, **possessive case** i.e.** 'one's'**, and its **reflexive case** i.e.** 'oneself' **will be used.
 
• **No other **objective, possessive or reflexive case will be used with** 'one'.**

**Thus, the correct sentence is**:* Our professor taught us that one should respect the religions of others as much as **one's** own. *

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Pronoun: A pronoun is a word that is used instead of a noun or noun phrase.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error,select 'No Error'.**

No sooner had she arrive that her (1)/ friends arranged a reception in her (2)/ honour in the best resort in the town. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of no sooner....than conjunction is being focused. When it is used in the sentence, then the verb is being followed according to the tense used further in the sentence. Since, **arranged **shows that it is a simple past tense. Hence, replace **had she arrive that **with **did she arrive than** to represent simple past tense. Also, the third form of 'arrive' will be applicable here. Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - No sooner did she arrive** than her friends arranged a reception in her honour in the best resort in the town.

questions.solution:

questions.solution:

• **Example:** The lights were **on or off** during the storm.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

I am definitely late, the bus** **(will have left) the bus stop by the time I reach there.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

Here, concept of conditionals is brought under consideration. There are two uses of phrase 'by the time' :-

***By the time*** is followed by a clause that relates a time-frame, for viewing the progress or completion of the activity in the main clause.

For e.g.:- The sun **will be setting** **by the time** I **get** home.

Whereas, it also includes an activity with duration and an end-point—possibly before and up to a fixed time. 

For e.g. :- The sun **will have set ****by the time **I **get** home.

Thus, that depends upon the meaning and sense of the sentence as well.

Hence, there is no grammatical error in given sentence. So, option 4 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence: **

I** **am definitely late, the bus** ***will have left *the bus stop by the time I reach there.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

**(Having had) **in the USA Embassy for a long time, Mr. Gupta has met many prominent personalities.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

Here, concept of participle is brought under consideration. Participle is V3 or V4 form of verb that can be used for joining two sentences. The first sentence is the introductory sentence and second is the consequent sentence. Since, options 1 & 3 are not the formats of participle. Hence, they are eliminated.

Now, when two sentences have the same subject and the duration between two actions performed by the subject is more, then following pattern is followed :- Having + V3 -> Same subject -> **duration more**. 

For e.g. :- The sun having risen, the people went for work.

But when, two sentences have the same subject and passive form of verb is used, then following pattern is followed :- Having + been + same subject -> Passive Voice. 

For e.g. :- Having been played, the kids slept.

Since, both the actions 'living in USA' and 'meeting prominent personalities' have little duration. Hence, option 4 is eliminated. Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Having been in the USA Embassy for a long time, Mr. Gupta has met many prominent personalities.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The guest stood quietly for** ****(few moments)**.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** "a few moments"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, concept of quantifiers such as** little **and **few** giving meaning of some is brought under consideration. 
 
• Following are the uses of these quantifiers :- 
 
• **Little**** **and **few**** **have **negative meanings**. They mean **limited or below average (hardly any).**
 
 
• ***Example: ****Few **students have attended the class today.*
 
 
 
• **A little** and** a few **mean some, **somewhat (though not that much).** It has a **positive meaning.**
 
 
• ***​Example: A few **students are absent.*
 
 
 
• **The little** and** the few** mean **'not much but all of that much available".**
 
 
• ***Example: The few **friends he had were all very helpful.*
 
 
 
• **​'Few'** is used with **plural nouns**.
 
• With reference to the context, guest is a person who is invited at other's place. Hence, he shows decency at someone's else place. So, he must have stood for some time. Thus, replace '**few' **with **'****a few' **to make the sentence contextually correct.
 
• Hence, **option 1 i.e.** **a few moments **is the correct answer.

 

**Correct sentence__ - ***The guest stood quietly for __**a few moments**__.*
